entries.title: Dr. Robotnik's Mean Bean Machine
entries.definitive_edition: Windows Steam/SEGA Classics Genesis version if owned; Nintendo Switch Online Genesis version is the current official fallback

emulation.emulator: Official SEGA Classics / Genesis emulator / 8-bit emulator
emulation.notes: Use the owned Windows SEGA Classics release or a Genesis emulator for the main version; use Game Gear/Master System/3DS VC for Puzzle Mode.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Genesis-version fidelity on PC for the main game; 8-bit native fidelity for Puzzle Mode.

primary.version: Steam / SEGA Classics Genesis version if owned
primary.why: The Genesis/Mega Drive original released alongside Game Gear and Master System versions, with later Wii, Windows, 3DS, and Nintendo Switch Online access routes. Windows/SEGA Classics is the best capture route for the Genesis version if already owned, while the 8-bit Game Gear/Master System route is secondary for Puzzle Mode.
primary.how_to_play: Use the owned Windows/Steam SEGA Classics release for the Genesis-version main playthrough. If it is not owned after the SEGA Classics delisting, use Nintendo Switch Online Genesis or original Genesis/emulation for the same main version, then play Puzzle Mode on Game Gear, Master System, or the 3DS Game Gear release.

secondary.exclusive_content: 8-bit versions with Puzzle Mode, a predetermined bean-clearing mode absent from the Genesis/Windows route.
secondary.what_to_play: After the Genesis-version main run, play Puzzle Mode on Game Gear, Master System, or the 3DS Game Gear Virtual Console release if already owned.
secondary.why: The Game Gear/Master System versions include Puzzle Mode, making the 8-bit route a content secondary.

entries.remaster_caveats: SEGA Classics titles, including Dr. Robotnik?s Mean Bean Machine on Steam, were delisted for new purchases after December 6, 2024, though owned copies remain playable; compilation appearances such as Sonic Mega Collection, Sonic?s Ultimate Genesis Collection, and Sonic Origins Plus are access routes rather than distinct primary versions.

entries.title: Good Friend Chao!
entries.definitive_edition: Original Sonic Cafe i-mode 504i release

emulation.emulator: Original 504i handset preferred; DoJa/i-mode preservation tooling only if a verified app dump exists
emulation.notes: The Sonic Cafe service is defunct and no modern port is sourced. Capture from original hardware or a verified preserved i-appli only; document any emulator/tooling gaps clearly.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Japanese 504i handset capture of the Sonic Cafe i-appli

primary.version: Original Japanese Sonic Cafe i-mode 504i release (Nakayoshi Chao!)
primary.why: No public release references page was found for this Sonic Cafe mobile title. Good Friend Chao! / Nakayoshi Chao! is a Japan-only Sonic Cafe i-appli for NTT DoCoMo 504i phones, with no console, PC, or modern mobile rerelease.
primary.how_to_play: There is no normal current purchase or public rerelease route. The archival target is an original compatible NTT DoCoMo 504i handset with the app preserved, or a verified preserved i-appli dump in a compatible DoJa/i-mode preservation environment if one becomes available. Without that, treat the entry as researched-but-not-currently-playable rather than substituting Chao Garden modes from other Sonic games.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not conflate this with Sonic Adventure's Chao Garden, Sonic Adventure 2's Chao Garden, or Tiny Chao Garden. DJcube reports no public ROM/app dump available, so preservation status is weaker than for normal retail releases.

entries.title: Knuckles' Chaotix

emulation.notes: Use an owned 32X cartridge dump. The Japan/USA and Europe ROMs are completable-unverified; 32X support is present, with typical 320x224/240 geometry.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Accurate 32X emulation or original hardware capture

primary.version: Original 32X cartridge or accurate 32X emulation
primary.why: the original SEGA 32X release exists, and the only later official availability was a brief, now-defunct GameTap rerelease. The 32X version is therefore the preservation baseline and the only currently practical route.
primary.how_to_play: Use an original 32X cartridge on real hardware for authenticity, or dump the cartridge and play via a 32X-capable emulator such as ares or RetroArch PicoDrive for clean capture. Avoid treating Sonic compilations as substitutes; Knuckles' Chaotix has not had a modern collection/remaster rerelease.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern official remaster or compilation rerelease was found. The brief GameTap Windows/Mac availability is defunct, so the 32X cartridge/dump remains the archive route.
